Also, apply it as a plaster, and apply bull's bile with two obols of opium. It is beneficial to fumigate the womb with stag hair. They relate that does, when they feel they are pregnant, swallow a small stone, which the owner keeps, once found in the excrement or in the womb (for it is found there too), and ties to the body. Small bones are also found in the heart and womb, very useful for pregnant women and those in labor. For the pumice stone, which is found in the uterus of cows in a similar way, we spoke of in the nature of cattle. Wolf fat applied softens the womb. It also prevails against the harmful effects of plasters applied to its pains. And it is not <unclear>beneficial.</unclear> Or if they are beginning to go into labor, it should be near what she has eaten. To the point that it prevails even against harmful applied plasters. And it is indeed a small thing to supervene. The use of the hare is great for women. Dried lung, drunk, aids the womb. For hemorrhages, drink the liver with Samian earth in water. For the afterbirth, rennet. They avoid daily baths. Also, when applied with saffron and leek juice, and inserted in wool, it expels dead fetuses. If the wombs of hares are eaten, they believe that males are conceived. They think this is also achieved by their testicles and rennet. That the conception of a hare, taken from the uterus, brings back fertility to those who have ceased to bear children. But the conception of a hare is also healthy, and the Magi give it to a man to drink. Likewise, nine grains of dung to a virgin, so that her breasts may stand perpetually. Also with rennet. For that reason, when mixed with honey, it is applied to the blood when they do not want pulled-out hairs to grow back again. For the inflation of the womb, it is beneficial to apply boar or pig dung with oil. It is more effective to stop it if the flour is dry or sprinkled into a drink, as if it torments a pregnant woman or a woman in labor. Swine's milk drunk with honeyed wine aids the labor of women. But drunk by itself, it replenishes the failing breasts of women who have given birth. The same, smeared with the blood of a female pig, causes them to grow less. If they ache, soothe them with the drinking of ass's milk. Which, taken with added honey, also aids their purgations. The old suet of the same animal heals ulcerations of the womb: and when applied in wool, it softens the hardness of the womb. But when applied fresh or old with water, it holds the power of a <term>psilothrum</term> <gloss>depilatory</gloss>. The old spleen of the same animal, applied with water, makes breasts abundant. It clears the face. Fumigated ass's hooves hasten labor, so that it may even call forth an abortion; nor is it applied otherwise than that it kills the living fetus. If the fresh dung of the same animal is applied, it is said to stop hemorrhages of blood miraculously. And also the ash of the same dung, which is also beneficial to the womb when applied. Mare's foam, applied for forty days before they are born, stops the first hairs. Likewise, stag's horn is learned. Or if the horns are fresh. Wombs are aided by being washed with mare's milk. But if the labor feels dead, the spleen drunk in sweet water expels it. Likewise, fumigation with hooves or dry dung. It checks drooping faces when infused with butter. Bull's bile, mixed with rose oil, opens a hardened womb, applied externally in wool with turpentine resin. They also say that by fumigating with dung from a bull, drooping wombs are restrained and labor is aided. But conception [is aided] by drinking cow's milk. It is certain that sterility occurs because of the vexation of labor. Olympias of Thebes affirms that this is corrected with bull's bile and the fat of serpents and verdigris, with honey added to the medicated parts before intercourse. They also promise that if they eat calf's meat roasted with birthwort around the time of conception, they will give birth to males. Calf marrow, boiled in wine and water with suet, is beneficial for ulcerations of the womb. Likewise, fox fat, and cat excrement applied with resin and rose oil. They think it most useful to fumigate the womb with goat horn. The blood of wild goats with sea palm pulls out hairs. But the bile of the others, when sprinkled, softens the calluses of the womb and makes conception possible after purgation. Thus also the power of the <term>psilothrum</term> <gloss>depilatory</gloss> is effected; it is kept applied for three days after the hairs are pulled out. Midwives promise that an immense hemorrhage is stopped if goat urine is drunk, and if the dung is applied. The membrane of goats, boiled in water and taken old in a drink in wine, expels the afterbirth. They think it useful to fumigate the womb with the hair of kids. And in a hemorrhage of blood, to drink rennet or apply henbane seed. If the loins of a black wild bull are pricked with goat blood, it is said that a weariness of sex is caused in the woman, says Aeschines. The same, goat urine drunk as a love potion, mixed with spikenard because of the aroma. For infants, nothing is more useful than butter, by itself and with honey, both privately in teething, and for the gums, and for sores of the mouth. A wolf's tooth tied to an infant prevents terrors and the diseases of teething. Which also the wolf's skin provides. Indeed, their largest teeth, when tied to horses, are said to provide an indefatigable speed. The belly of infants is stopped by rabbit rennet applied to the breast. Ass's liver, instilled into the mouth with a little all-heal mixed in, protects infants from epileptic diseases and others. They instruct that this be done for forty days. And ass's skin thrown over them makes infants fearless. The teeth that first fall from horses provide easy teething for infants when tied to them. More effectively if they have not touched the ground. Calf's spleen should be eaten in honey. And applied for pain of the spleen. For flowing ulcers with honey. Calf's spleen boiled in wine and crushed and applied [cures] small ulcers of the mouth. Goat brain, passed through a gold ring before milk is given to infants, should be instilled against epilepsy and other diseases of infants. Goat dung tied in a cloth restrains restless infants, especially girls. Gums smeared with goat's milk or hare's brain make teething easy. Cato thinks that sleep is induced if hare is taken in food. The common people also think it gives grace to the body for nine days in the same place. To which, however, some cause must underlie such a great persuasion. The Magi say that sleep is induced if the bile of a sacrificed goat is applied only to the eyes or placed under the pillow. Ash of goat horn, smeared with myrtle oil, inhibits sweats. But boar's bile, applied, stimulates intercourse. Likewise, swine marrow drunk. Ass's suet mixed with the fat of a male goose, applied. Likewise from the intercourse of horses, according to Virgil
